stages.name: Frontier
stages.summary: One client does everything: P2P, PoW mining, EVM execution, state storage. Blocks start at 5,000 gas.
changes: Ethash PoW (proof of work) with a difficulty bomb
EVM: stack machine that runs gas-metered bytecode
World state in a hexary Merkle-Patricia trie
devp2p networking on TCP port 30303
Two account types: EOA and contract
stages.bookNote: Chapter 1 lists these components: P2P network, consensus rules, transactions, state machine, data structures, clients.

stages.name: Homestead → Spurious Dragon
stages.sub: Homestead, DAO fork, Tangerine Whistle, Spurious Dragon
stages.summary: Four 2016 forks harden the chain. Homestead stabilises it, the DAO fork reverses the DAO hack, and two forks fix DoS attacks. The architecture stays the same.
changes: Homestead: EIP-2 safer creation, EIP-7 DELEGATECALL
DAO fork (Jul 2016): irregular state change; Ethereum Classic splits off
Tangerine Whistle: EIP-150 reprices IO opcodes after DoS attacks
Spurious Dragon: EIP-155 replay protection with chain ID
Spurious Dragon: EIP-170 24 KB contract size limit; EIP-161 state clearing
stages.bookNote: Chapter 1 names EIP-2, EIP-7 and EIP-8 as the key Homestead changes. Chapter 3 mentions the 2016 DoS attacks. The book does not name Tangerine Whistle or Spurious Dragon; EELS has a folder for each.

stages.name: Byzantium + Constantinople
stages.summary: Metropolis adds new opcodes and the first zk-SNARK precompiles. Block rewards drop and the difficulty bomb moves back.
changes: REVERT, STATICCALL, RETURNDATA opcodes
alt_bn128 precompiles: on-chain zk-SNARK checks
CREATE2 (EIP-1014): addresses known before deploy
Bitwise shift opcodes SHL, SHR, SAR
Block reward 5 → 3 → 2 ETH
stages.bookNote: Chapter 1 groups Byzantium, Constantinople and Istanbul under Metropolis. Chapter 14 covers CREATE vs CREATE2.

stages.name: Istanbul
stages.summary: Calldata gets 4x cheaper and zk precompiles get cheaper. This makes the first rollup designs viable on L1.
changes: EIP-2028: calldata 68 → 16 gas per non-zero byte
EIP-1108: cheaper alt_bn128 precompiles
EIP-1344: CHAINID opcode
EIP-1884: repricing of state-access opcodes
stages.bookNote: Chapter 1 credits Istanbul with zk support for scaling and privacy.

stages.name: Beacon + London
stages.summary: A separate PoS chain (the Beacon Chain) starts beside the PoW chain. The PoW chain gets typed transactions and the EIP-1559 fee market.
changes: Beacon Chain genesis (1 Dec 2020): validators deposit 32 ETH
Berlin: typed tx envelope (EIP-2718) and access lists (EIP-2930)
London: EIP-1559 base fee is burned, tip goes to producer
Altair: sync committees for light clients
Optimistic rollups go live on calldata
stages.bookNote: Chapter 6 explains type 0x01 and 0x02 transactions. Chapter 15 explains the Beacon Chain and Gasper.

stages.name: The Merge
stages.summary: PoW stops. A node is now two programs: a consensus client and an execution client, joined by the Engine API.
changes: Ethash removed; Gasper (LMD-GHOST + Casper FFG) secures the chain
Node = consensus client + execution client
Engine API links the two clients
12-second slots, 32-slot epochs, finality in ~2 epochs
MEV-Boost relays and builders appear off-protocol
stages.bookNote: Chapter 3 shows the two-client node (Figure 3-1). Chapter 15 explains slots, epochs, justification and finality.

stages.name: Shapella
stages.summary: Staked ETH can leave the Beacon Chain. Withdrawals finish the Merge.
changes: EIP-4895: validator withdrawals to EL addresses
EIP-3855: PUSH0 opcode
EIP-3860: limit on initcode size
ERC-4337 smart accounts launch at the app layer (Mar 2023)

stages.name: Dencun
stages.summary: Proto-danksharding adds blobs: a second data lane for rollups with its own fee market. Blobs travel on the consensus layer and expire after ~18 days.
changes: EIP-4844: blob transactions (type 0x03), target 3 / max 6 blobs
KZG commitments from the KZG ceremony
EIP-1153 TSTORE/TLOAD and EIP-5656 MCOPY
EIP-6780: SELFDESTRUCT only works in the same tx
EIP-4788: beacon block root inside the EVM
stages.bookNote: Chapter 4 explains KZG commitments. Chapter 16 explains proto-danksharding and why blobs expire.

stages.name: Pectra
stages.summary: EOAs can run contract code. Validators can hold up to 2,048 ETH. Blob capacity doubles. This is the last fork the book covers in full.
changes: EIP-7702: EOAs delegate to contract code (type 0x04)
EIP-7251: max effective balance 32 → 2,048 ETH
EIP-7002 + EIP-6110: exits and deposits triggered from the EL
EIP-7691: blobs target 6 / max 9
EIP-7623: higher calldata floor; EIP-2537: BLS precompile
stages.bookNote: Chapter 14 explains the 0xef0100 delegation designator. Book snapshot ends June 2025, one month after Pectra.

stages.name: Fusaka
stages.summary: Nodes stop downloading every blob. PeerDAS lets each node keep and sample a subset of data columns. Blob limits now rise through small BPO forks.
changes: EIP-7594 PeerDAS: data availability sampling by peers
EIP-7892 BPO forks: BPO1 10/15 (9 Dec 2025), BPO2 14/21 (7 Jan 2026)
EIP-7935: default gas limit 60M; EIP-7825: tx gas cap 2^24
EIP-7951 secp256r1 precompile (passkeys); EIP-7939 CLZ opcode
EIP-7917 proposer lookahead; EIP-7918 blob base fee floor
stages.bookNote: After the book. Chapter 16 describes DAS as a danksharding goal; PeerDAS is the first live form of it.

stages.name: Glamsterdam
stages.summary: Block building moves into the protocol (ePBS). Blocks carry an access list so clients can validate transactions in parallel. Meta EIP-7773 schedules 18 core EIPs. Sepolia forked 6 Oct 2026; the Hoodi fork is on hold over gas-repricing risks.
changes: EIP-7732 ePBS: builders bid in-protocol; Payload Timeliness Committee
EIP-7928 Block-Level Access Lists: parallel validation and state prefetch
Gas model: EIP-2780, 7778, 7976, 7981, 8037, 8038 (state costs more, refunds leave block accounting)
EVM and accounts: EIP-7843 SLOTNUM, 8024 SWAPN/DUPN, 7954 larger contracts, 7708 ETH transfers emit logs
Validators: EIP-8045, 8061, 8282; networking: eth/70, eth/71, eth/72 sparse blobpool
stages.bookNote: Chapter 14 lists ePBS as a step toward statelessness. Chapter 16 explains PBS and parallel execution as open research; both now have specs.

stages.name: Hegotá
stages.summary: Censorship resistance becomes a protocol rule (FOCIL). Accounts choose their own validation logic (frame transactions). The rest of the scope is still open.
changes: EIP-7805 FOCIL: committee inclusion lists, enforced by fork choice
EIP-8141 frame transactions: native account abstraction
Frame txs allow post-quantum signature schemes
Other EIPs only under consideration (meta EIP-8081)
stages.bookNote: After the book. Chapter 5 ends with 'the future of account abstraction'; frame transactions are the current answer.

stages.name: Lean Ethereum
stages.summary: A multi-fork redesign of all three layers: lean consensus, lean data, lean execution. Validators verify zk proofs instead of re-executing blocks.
changes: Binary state tree (EIP-7864) replaces the hexary MPT
zkEVM real-time proofs: verify, do not re-execute
Lean consensus: faster finality, shorter slots, PQ signatures
Full danksharding: far more blob space for L2s
Possible VM change (RISC-V) is still contested
stages.bookNote: Chapter 16 describes Verkle trees for statelessness. Current plans favour a binary hash tree; the book's note on 'other hash-based binary trees' anticipated this.

slots.label: EOA
ev: Holds ETH. Signs txs with one secp256k1 key. Cannot hold code.
EIP-7702: EOA sets 0xef0100 + address and runs that contract's code. Type 0x04 tx.
EIP-8141: account runs its own validation. Any signature scheme, incl. post-quantum.

slots.label: Contract account
ev: Code + storage. Runs only when a tx or call reaches it.
EIP-6780: code deletion only in the creating tx.
EIP-7954 raises max contract size. EIP-7708: ETH transfers emit a log.

slots.label: Smart accounts
ev: UserOps, bundlers, EntryPoint contract. No fork needed.
An EOA keeps its address and delegates to smart-account code.
Frame txs move validation into the account. Gas sponsors are native.

slots.label: Block producer
ev: Picks and orders txs, then mines the block with Ethash.
A random validator proposes each 12 s slot. Miners removed.
ePBS: beacon block commits to a builder's payload header.

slots.label: Builder market
ev: Builders bid through trusted relays. Most blocks come from a few builders.
Builders are in-protocol. A Payload Timeliness Committee checks the reveal.

slots.label: Inclusion guarantee
ev: A validator committee lists txs that must go in. Fork choice enforces it.

slots.label: Consensus
ev: Heaviest chain wins. Difficulty bomb pushes toward PoS.
Beacon Chain runs PoS beside PoW. Not linked to execution yet.
Fork choice + finality gadget. Finality after ~2 epochs (~12.8 min).
EIP-7917: proposer schedule fixed one epoch ahead.
Fast finality (seconds), shorter slots, post-quantum signatures.

slots.label: Validators & stake
ev: Deposit contract on the PoW chain. No withdrawals yet.
EIP-4895: partial and full withdrawals to EL addresses.
EIP-7251 consolidation. EIP-7002 exits and EIP-6110 deposits from the EL.
EIP-8061 churn up. EIP-8282 builder requests. EIP-8045 slashed cannot propose.
Lean design: hash-based PQ signatures, aggregated with SNARKs.

slots.label: Light clients
ev: 512 validators sign headers. Light clients follow the chain cheaply.
zk proofs + binary tree: verify the chain on a phone.

slots.label: CL networking
ev: Blocks and attestations on a separate P2P stack.
Full blobs travel next to beacon blocks.
PeerDAS: each node custodies some columns and samples others.
PTC votes on timely payload reveal (ePBS).
Heze spec: InclusionList messages from the IL committee.

slots.label: EVM
ev: EIP-7: run callee code in caller context.
Transient storage. EVM sees blob hashes, not blobs.
Blocks carry proofs. A RISC-V VM is a contested option.

slots.label: State tree
ev: Hexary, Keccak. World state in LevelDB.
EIP-2935: last 8,191 block hashes in a system contract.
Replaces MPT. Shorter proofs. Verkle plan dropped.

slots.label: Block validation
ev: Every node re-runs every tx in order.
EIP-7928: block lists every slot it touches.

slots.label: Block gas limit
ev: Lifted Sep 2015. Miners vote it up.

slots.label: Fee market
ev: Legacy tx. Fee goes to miner.

slots.label: EL networking
ev: Blocks now arrive from the CL.
Partial receipts. BAL exchange. BAL-based state healing.

slots.label: Mempool
ev: Any node gossips pending txs. Producer orders them.
Builders buy private flow. MEV extraction.
Blob txs carry cell proofs for PeerDAS.
EIP-8070: nodes keep part of each blob tx.
FOCIL committee picks txs from its local view.

slots.label: Data lane
ev: All data sits in execution blocks forever.
EIP-2028: 16 gas per byte. Rollups become viable.
EIP-4844. ~128 KB each, KZG commitment, pruned after ~18 days.
2D sampling. Many more blobs per slot.

slots.label: How nodes check data
ev: Custody a subset. Erasure code fills gaps.

slots.label: Layer 2
ev: Early L2 designs. Data stays off-chain.
L2 fees drop. Blob market separate from gas.
BPO forks scale capacity between named forks.

slots.label: Who verifies what
ev: Full state on disk (~1.2 TB by 2025).
Validators keep only the state root.

b2n: miner seals block (PoW) in the same client
proposer gets block from a builder via relay
builder bid committed in the beacon block (ePBS)
ePBS + inclusion lists enforced by fork choice
n2d: columns custodied and sampled by peers

sources: The Block: binary tree EIP-7864 + VM plan
